text: Leaves are created, so the signal does not remain on one, but it creates several copies of itself because of this hitting the obstacle. That's the so-called diffraction. Now, these different copies of the signal will then further proceed, and the same happens when our signal gets reflected. Also, reflection actually creates not multiple copies of the same signal, but a signal that hits a surface and then changes direction and further proceeds toward the receiver. So both diffraction and reflection have in common the fact that our signal or signals get in a way diverted, so they change direction, and then further proceed to the destination. But diffraction in particular then happens when several copies are created, is in a way more serious than reflection because it's not just the fact that the signal changes direction, but the signal actually transforms itself from one.
